title: Routing: enforce staged rollout traffic weights for Dedicated pools (deterministic + tenant-isolated)
creator: Jordan Lee
project: Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools
description:
Background
Dedicated staged rollouts introduce per-stage traffic weights (e.g., 5% canary / 95% stable) with strict tenant isolation and predictable behavior. Today routing for Dedicated pool updates is effectively pool-level / manual; for v1 we need deterministic weight enforcement so that:
- traffic allocation respects stage weights exactly (within sampling error)
- allocation is deterministic for a given request routing key + plan version (debuggable, repeatable)
- any multi-tenant routing components do not allow cross-tenant influence (seed/key isolation)

Scope (this ticket)
Implement routing-layer support to apply RolloutPlan stage weights for Dedicated pools.
- Input: control-plane returns active rollout state for a given Dedicated pool/route (active plan version + stage weights + which stage corresponds to which target config/model/runtime).
- Output: router deterministically selects a stage target per request and forwards to the appropriate backend, while maintaining Dedicated tenant isolation.

Non-goals
- Implementing gate evaluation (ENG-5124)
- Building the Console UI (ENG-5127)
- Building autoscaling headroom rules (ENG-5130) beyond a minimal “don’t route to 0% stage” invariant

Requirements / Acceptance Criteria
1) Deterministic selection
- For a given (tenant_id, pool_id, route_id, rollout_plan_id, plan_version, routing_key), stage selection is stable across router replicas and across time.
- No dependence on local RNG.

2) Weight enforcement
- Given stage weights W across stages in an active plan, selection probability approximates W within ±1% absolute error over >=100k requests (synthetic test).
- Support 0% and 100% weights.

3) Tenant isolation
- Hash key MUST include tenant_id and pool_id so identical routing_keys across tenants/pools cannot correlate.
- Ensure we only ever fetch/apply rollout plans for the resolved (tenant_id, pool_id) context.

4) Safe behavior on partial failures
- If rollout metadata is missing/invalid (e.g., sum(weights)=0, unknown stage target), fail closed to “stable target” if available; otherwise return 503 with explicit error tag (do not silently route to arbitrary stage).
- If stage weights are present but stage target is not ready/registered, treat that stage as 0% and emit a metric (to avoid blackholing a canary during activation races).

5) Observability
- Emit per-pool/route counters: requests_by_selected_stage, requests_by_effective_stage (after any override), and stage_selection_errors.
- Include rollout_plan_id + plan_version as low-cardinality labels only (no user/request ids).

Implementation plan
A) Routing key / stickiness
- Primary routing_key: request.header["x-redwood-rollout-key"] if present.
- Fallback routing_key: request_id (UUID) (sufficient for deterministic sampling even without session stickiness).
- Documented for operators: provide rollout-key for workloads that benefit from stickiness (e.g., chat sessions).

B) Deterministic weighted selection algorithm
- Compute h = HMAC-SHA256(seed, concat(tenant_id, pool_id, route_id, rollout_plan_id, plan_version, routing_key))
- Convert h[0:8] to uint64 and map to bucket in [0, 9999].
- Select stage via cumulative weights in basis points.
Notes:
- seed is control-plane provided “assignment_seed” per plan_version to prevent accidental coupling across plan versions and to support reproducible debugging.
- Using basis points avoids float drift and makes 0/100% exact.

C) Plan versioning and transitions
- Routing uses plan_version from control plane. If plan_version changes, reassignment occurs (expected).
- Guard 0%/100% transitions: treat weights array as authoritative; ensure cumulative math handles empty/zero cases.

D) Target resolution
- Stage target is a “ServingTargetRef” (model/runtime/config) resolved to a concrete backend cluster within the Dedicated pool.
- If resolution fails, treat stage weight as 0% for that request and re-run selection over remaining stages (stable-first preference). Emit metric stage_target_unavailable.

E) Overrides / headroom
- Minimal in this ticket: no capacity-aware override. (Autoscaling headroom + queue-depth overrides are tracked in ENG-5130.)
- Add a TODO hook (feature-flagged) to support “override-to-stable” signals later without changing the deterministic assignment code path.

Testing
- Unit tests:
  - Determinism across replicas (fixed seed + inputs => same stage)
  - Distribution tests for a few weight vectors (5/95, 25/75, 33/33/34)
  - 0% and 100% edge cases
  - Missing target resolution => reselect and metric increment
- Integration tests (staging):
  - Router consumes rollout metadata, enforces weights, and reports metrics
  - Plan version bump causes expected reassignment (and metrics reflect new plan_version)
- Load test (linked): sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/infrastructure/dedicated-rollout-load-test-plan.json

Rollout plan
- Ship behind feature flag: dedicated.staged_rollouts_routing_enabled (per-tenant allowlist).
- Dogfood on Redwood-managed Dedicated pools first.
- Enable for 1 internal tenant + 1 enterprise beta after SRE signoff on dashboards.

Links
- Epic: PM-418
- Related eng tickets: ENG-5121 (control-plane objects), ENG-5122 (rollout APIs), ENG-5124 (gate evaluator), ENG-5130 (autoscaling guardrails)
- GitHub: sources/github/redwood/pr_28479.json (routing integration PR)
comments: 2025-01-08 — Elena Popov: Drafted routing selection approach. Proposing HMAC(seed, stable identifiers + routing_key) mapped to basis points; avoids per-replica RNG differences. Need confirmation from Jordan on which identifiers MUST be included for isolation (tenant_id/pool_id at minimum).

2025-01-09 — Jordan Lee: +1 on HMAC + basis points. Please include plan_version in the hash input so assignment is stable within a version and changes are explainable when version bumps. Also: do NOT include stage_id in the hash input (it breaks when stages are re-ordered); selection should be done by cumulative weights over ordered stage list.

2025-01-11 — Mina Haddad: Re: tenant isolation — Dedicated pools are per-tenant, but router is shared. Ensure cache keys for rollout state are scoped by (tenant_id,pool_id,route_id) to avoid accidental bleed between tenants if bugs occur. Also confirm “route_id” exists in all Dedicated requests; otherwise use derived key (model_route_name).

2025-01-14 — Elena Popov: Implemented cache scoping by (tenant_id,pool_id,route_id). Added fallback to route_name when route_id missing (older agents). Added metric rollout_routing_context_missing_route_id to track if this is common; may need cleanup later.

2025-01-18 — Sean Gallagher: From SRE side, we need clear metrics for “selection errors” and “target unavailable -> reselect” because those are early indicators of control-plane/routing races. Please ensure labels remain low-cardinality; plan_id and version are OK, but no stage_name strings if they’re dynamic.

2025-01-20 — Elena Popov: Adjusted metrics: use stage_index (int) rather than stage_name to keep labels stable/low-cardinality. plan_id and plan_version labels only. Added a separate structured log line at debug level with stage_name for oncall when needed.

2025-01-24 — Elena Popov: Open question: if all stages are unavailable (target resolution fails), I currently fail closed to 503 with reason=rollout_target_unavailable. Alternative is to route to “last known stable” even if target resolution fails. Mina suggested 503 is better than silently routing wrong target. Leaving as 503; revisit if this causes noisy incidents.
2025-01-28 — Elena Popov: PR up for review (routing integration). Includes determinism tests + distribution test. Link: sources/github/redwood/pr_28479.json

2025-01-29 — Mina Haddad: Approved. Looks good. Follow-up: add a hook for capacity-aware override once ENG-5130 lands, but keep deterministic assignment vs effective routing separate (record both in metrics). Marking ticket Done.
